targets.summary: Balance is read before the awaits and written back after, so concurrent ticks lose updates.
discount is optional on the row but dereferenced unguarded, throwing for carts with no coupon.
settledAt is a nullable TypeORM column, so an unsettled row loads as null rather than undefined, and isSettled() returns true for every unsettled invoice.
The directory Map starts empty; get returns undefined for a missing id, then displayName dereferences name.
couponFor forwards resolveCoupon, which returns undefined; discount dereferences amount.

config.note: Development experiment of internal calls only. Same saved source/policy, fresh CLI calls. No release or end-to-end claim.

findings.reason: tick() reads ledger.balanceOf/settledSince then later calls ledger.write(account.id, adjusted); backfill() independently reads entriesSince/balanceOf for the same account and also calls ledger.write. Both are exported methods that can run concurrently (periodic tick loop vs. an on-demand backfill/retry call), so a write from one can overwrite the other's stale-read-derived balance, leaving the led…

row.lines is defensively defaulted to [] on the previous line, showing the author expects cart rows to have missing/optional sub-objects, but row.discount is dereferenced directly as row.discount.amount with no such guard; a cart row without a discount object (the same shape of omission handled for lines) throws TypeError reading 'amount' of undefined.
All five functions are exact duplicates performing the same trim/passthrough logic; this is redundant code but produces no observably wrong return value or side effect for any input.

settledAt is declared with `@Column({ nullable: true })`, meaning TypeORM materializes an unset value as `null` when read back from the database, not `undefined`. isSettled() checks `this.settledAt !== undefined`, so a genuinely unsettled invoice loaded from the DB (settledAt === null) incorrectly returns true.

directory.get delegates to rows.get(id) on a Map<string, {name:string}>, whose contract returns undefined for any id not present; displayName immediately calls .name.toUpperCase() on that result with no guard, so a valid lookup miss throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined'.

couponFor is backed by resolveCoupon, typed to return `{amount:number} | undefined`, and shown returning undefined for a valid id with no match; discount() calls couponFor(id).amount without checking for undefined, so a normal lookup miss throws when reading 'amount'.
Uses optional chaining (?.name) and a nullish-coalescing fallback (?? "Unknown"), correctly handling the Map.get() undefined case shown in the callee contract.
Uses optional chaining (?.amount) and a nullish-coalescing fallback (?? 0), correctly handling the undefined return shown in resolveCoupon's contract.
